questions.question: How do MVC and routing fit together in Rails?
questions.title: MVC and Routing in Rails
questions.direct_answer: MVC splits an app into Model (data + logic: Post, User), View (presentation: index.html.erb, JSON), Controller (orchestration: PostsController). Routing is the entry point: config/routes.rb maps a URL + verb to a controller#action (get '/posts/:id', to: 'posts#show'). So the flow is: request -> router -> controller -> model -> view -> response. The model owns rules and data; the view owns presentation; the controller wires them. Rails' convention over configuration means a Post model, PostsController, and views/posts/ all line up automatically — you write little glue. resources :posts wires the 7 REST routes for you.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you can name M/V/C's jobs (model: data+logic; view: presentation; controller: orchestration) and how routing maps URLs to actions.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Putting presentation in the model (model knows HTML) or business logic in the view — break the separation.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: MVC: Model (data+logic), View (presentation), Controller (orchestration). Routing maps URL+verb to controller#action. Rails' convention wires them automatically.

sections.title: Request through MVC
sections.content:
router -> controller -> model -> view -> response; routes.rb maps URLs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[router: routes.rb] --> C[controller]
  C --> M[model: data + logic]
  M --> V[view: presentation]
  V --> Re[response]
```

sections.title: MVC and routing
sections.content:
```ruby # config/routes.rb (routing: URL + verb -> controller#action) Rails.application.routes.draw do get '/posts/:id', to: 'posts#show' # GET /posts/42 -> PostsController#show resources :posts # the 7 REST routes end # Model (app/models/post.rb): data + logic class Post < ApplicationRecord validates :title, presence: true def published?; published_at.present?; end end # Controller (app/controllers/posts_controller.rb): orchestration class PostsController < ApplicationController def show @post = Post.find(params[:id]) # ask the model # render app/views/posts/show.html.erb (convention) end end # View (app/views/posts/show.html.erb): presentation #

<%= @post.title %>

```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Putting presentation in the model (the model shouldn't know HTML).
Business logic in the view — break the separation; keep views dumb.
Not knowing routes.rb maps URLs to actions (the entry point of MVC).

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: Routing maps a URL + verb to a controller#action in routes.rb.
Flow: request -> router -> controller -> model -> view -> response.
Rails' convention over configuration aligns Post/PostsController/views/posts.
resources :posts wires the 7 REST routes; the model owns rules, the view owns presentation.
